note: Accessory power (formerly magical power) granted by one accessory, by rarity, plus the three accessories the game scores differently. Hand-entered: the items resource exposes an accessory's rarity but not its accessory power. Everything else in the accessory model is API-derived.
source: Hypixel SkyBlock community wiki, Accessory Power/Mechanics and Template:Max AP
rarityOrderNote: The ladder a Recombobulator climbs, which is not every rarity that exists. Divine, Ultimate and Admin have a magical power above but are deliberately off the ladder: no Recombobulator reaches them, and putting Divine after Mythic offered every mythic accessory a step up to 28 that nobody can take.

excludedItems.note: Empty on purpose. Several bag items (party hats, cake bag) are classified ACCESSORY by the items resource, and nothing in the API says whether they grant magical power. Excluding them on a hunch would hide buyable XP; the computed-vs-reported MP readout is the check instead.

climbing.note: Accessories whose rarity climbs in place, through their own mechanic rather than by being bought. The items resource states where each one starts and nothing states where it ends, so the catalogue could only ever offer the base rarity and the one Recombobulator step after it. The rest is real XP that no purchase can reach, and it belongs in the browser as a grind rather than being left out of the total.
climbing.source: Read off the bag of a profile sitting at the documented maximum of 2,122 accessory power. Every rarity here is one a real player is holding — stated by the item, not claimed by a table — which is what makes it a maximum rather than a guess. Where the item was also recombobulated, that step is inside the figure.
climbing.consequence: Too high and the browser offers XP nobody can reach; too low and a maxed bag reads as short. The check is that the profile these came from reconciles to 2,122 exactly with nothing outstanding.

items.by: twelve perfect gemstones, then a Recombobulator

riftPrism.by: imbued at Erihann, which consumes the prism and pays for good

knownGaps: highest_magical_power is a high-water mark, not a current reading, so computed MP can sit below it legitimately.

All three special cases are modelled now: Hegemony doubles its own MP, an Abicase adds 1 per 2 Abiphone contacts, and an imbued Rift Prism is worth 11 whether or not it is still in the bag (the profile records it as rift.access.consumed_prism, since imbuing consumes it).

Contacts are counted from active_contacts, not contact_data. The two disagree: contact_data holds only the contacts with state attached and read 80 against a real 84 on the profile this was checked against, which is 2 MP.

Against a maxed profile reporting 2,122 MP in game the model now reads 2,122 exactly, and offers that player nothing at all as still missing. Ruled out along the way, by measurement rather than argument: dungeon accessories counting double (overshoots to 2,216), enrichments (the wiki's Enrichments page never mentions magical power), and Personal Deletor 6000 vs 7000 being separate families (the wiki states 7000 upgrades_from 6000, so merging them is right).

Accessories whose rarity climbs through play — Book of Progression, Pandora's Box, Pulse Ring, Relic of Power, Trapper Crest — are far below their real rarity in the items resource. The item's own lore carries the truth and is what scoreBag reads. The *unowned* ones are still priced off the resource, so their share of the ceiling is understated: nothing published says what rarity a player would end up at, and assuming the maximum would sell XP that takes a mechanic rather than coins.
A rarity the byRarity table has no figure for falls back to the resource rather than scoring nil, so a lore line we have not seen before cannot silently zero an accessory.
